title: Bollywood Stars Rally Behind Sonam Wangchuk as Hunger Strike Enters Third Week
excerpt: Swara Bhasker visits protest site as Shabana Azmi, Naseeruddin Shah, Sonakshi Sinha and others make emotional appeals urging the activist to end his fast.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Activist Sonam Wangchuk has been on hunger strike at Jantar Mantar for over 17 days
  • Swara Bhasker visited the protest site and expressed solidarity with the cause
  • Shabana Azmi, Soni Razdan and Sonakshi Sinha have made public appeals for Wangchuk to end his fast
  • The Cockroach Janta Party is demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over NEET irregularities
  • A march to Parliament is planned for July 20, coinciding with the start of the Monsoon Session
Environmental activist and education reformer Sonam Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi has entered its third week, drawing a growing wave of support from Bollywood celebrities who are using their platforms to amplify his cause — even as they plead with him to preserve his health. ## Swara Bhasker Joins the Protest Actress Swara Bhasker, known for her vocal stance on social issues, visited the protest site on Tuesday to meet Wangchuk and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke. Photographs shared on the CJP's official Instagram account showed Bhasker at Jantar Mantar. "Thank you for fighting for the future of all of our children," Bhasker wrote in her Instagram Stories, addressing Dipke. For Wangchuk, she called him "indefatigable" and said her "full solidarity" was with his struggle for children's futures. ## Health Concerns Mount Wangchuk, who began his fast on June 28, has lost approximately 8.2 kilograms and is beginning to lose muscle mass, according to Dipke. The deterioration in his health has prompted a Public Interest Litigation in the Delhi High Court seeking urgent medical intervention. This has made the appeals from the film industry increasingly urgent. Actress Soni Razdan — Alia Bhatt's mother — shared an emotional post on Instagram: "Dear Sonam Wangchuk, we all pray for your good health. Please do not leave us like this. You need to survive to fight the battle ahead." Veteran actress Shabana Azmi, actors Naseeruddin Shah and Ratna Pathak Shah, and writer Arundhati Roy have issued a joint statement urging the CJP to end the hunger strike: "This battle is a marathon, not a sprint, and we need you, your strength and leadership in the days to come." ## The NEET Demand The CJP has been rallying at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, citing alleged irregularities in the NEET examination process. The movement has announced plans for a "Chalo Sansad" march to Parliament on July 20, coinciding with the start of the Monsoon Session. Actor-filmmaker Imran Khan and actresses Sonakshi Sinha and Fatima Sana Shaikh have also voiced support, with Sinha criticising public silence around Wangchuk's concerns and calling for more voices to join the cause. ## Why the Diaspora Is Watching For Indians abroad, the NEET controversy resonates on multiple levels. Many NRI families have children who take competitive exams in India or are considering Indian universities, and the integrity of the examination system matters to them directly. Wangchuk himself, as the inspiration behind the film "3 Idiots," has a profile that extends well beyond India's borders. The growing celebrity support — and the parallel concern over Wangchuk's health — has turned what began as a niche protest into a national conversation about education, accountability and the limits of activism.
